chunks: From him, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskhan, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about 'those with the 'irbah among men'. He said, 'He is the foolish one who does not approach women.'

key_terms.أُولِي الْإِرْبَةِ: Those possessing 'irbah (a term related to procreation or the act of impregnating)

ai.seo_question: What does 'uli al-irbah' mean in Shia jurisprudence regarding men and childbirth?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that 'uli al-irbah' (those with financial means or capacity) refers specifically to the 'ahmaq' (foolish one) who abstains from marital intimacy despite having the means, rather than merely being wealthy. This definition is crucial for determining the waiting period (iddah) and financial maintenance (nafaqah) of a wife, as her status depends on whether her husband is capable of consummating the marriage. The term highlights a spiritual or practical deficiency in fulfilling marital duties, linking financial capacity with the ability to procreate.
